newsitem.title: USA: Reno reviews campaign finance investigation request.
newsitem.headline: Reno reviews campaign finance investigation request.

text.p: The Justice Department is reviewing requests by five congressional Republicans for an independent counsel to investigate allegations the Democrats accepted improper foreign donations, Attorney General Janet Reno said on Thursday.

"We just received the requests ... and we are looking at it in the context of the independent counsel statute," she said at her weekly Justice Department news conference. Five senior Republican lawmakers on Tuesday wrote to Reno, asking her for an independent counsel to investigate eight specific allegations of federal election violations.

Among the incidents cited were the Democratic Party's receipt of $425,000 from an Indonesian couple with links to the financial conglomerate Lippo Group and Democratic National Committee official John Huang's fundraising activities.

Sen. John McCain and four House Republicans asked Reno for an expedited answer, no later than Friday. But she refused to commit herself to a Friday decision, saying the law sets its own deadlines on when action must be taken.
"We will try to keep them advised of just what we're doing consistent with the way we conduct investigations," she said.

In another development on Thursday, a federal judge granted Huang's request to end face-to-face questioning by a conservative legal group in a freedom-of-information case over Commerce Department trade missions. The Judicial Watch group questioned Huang, a former Commerce Department official, for more than five hours on Tuesday.
Huang's attorneys moved to end the deposition, calling the questioning abusive. U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth agreed, saying any further questions must be submitted in writing.

McCain, a key supporter of Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, had asked Reno for an independent counsel and the citizens' lobbying group Common Cause made its own request after alleging violations of campaign finance laws by both political parties.

Reno said the requests have been referred to the Justice Department's public integrity section, where career lawyers are familiar with campaign finance laws. Asked if anyone at the White House talked to her about the requests, she replied, "No."

She rejected charges the department has delayed a decision about Huang, who has come under fire over the legality of campaign contributions he solicited from Asian Americans. She said she has tried to make sure proper procedures have been put in place, "and they don't change just because there is an election."

"I get criticised for doing one thing. I get criticised if I don't do another thing. You're damned if you do and damned if you don't. Facing those alternatives, I've just decided to do it the best way I can consistent with the evidence, the law (and) the statute," she said.
